hints.title: Ratio Inversion
hints.text: Rewrite nums[p] * nums[r] == nums[q] * nums[s] as nums[p] / nums[q] == nums[s] / nums[r].

hints.title: Greatest Common Divisor Reduction
hints.text: Reduce ratios to irreducible fraction pairs (a / gcd(a, b), b / gcd(a, b)).

hints.title: Two-Dimensional Meet-in-the-Middle
hints.text: Iterate r, dynamically adding all valid (p, q) ratios for q = r - 2, then querying (s, r) pairs.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import math
from collections import defaultdict

class Solution:
    def numberOfSubsequences(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        ans = 0
        left_ratios = defaultdict(int)
        
        for r in range(4, n - 2):
            q = r - 2
            for p in range(0, q - 1):
                g = math.gcd(nums[p], nums[q])
                left_ratios[(nums[p] // g, nums[q] // g)] += 1
                
            for s in range(r + 2, n):
                g = math.gcd(nums[s], nums[r])
                ans += left_ratios[(nums[s] // g, nums[r] // g)]
                
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Reduces quadruplets into pairs of irreducible fraction ratios in O(n^2).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all quadruplets takes O(n^4) which times out.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n^2) hash map stores irreducible ratio counts.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Rewrites product condition into normalized ratios and uses dynamic frequency counting.
